text:
kevin: quick question — before we ship the adaptive quant rollout, can we agree on a minimal set of runtime sanity checks + fallback actions?

sasha: yes. we need something lightweight that won't add much tail latency. 

maria: agreed. baseline idea: golden prompt set (50 short prompts) + p95 token-delta threshold per-model. if delta > X, trigger fallback.

jordan: how do we compute "token-delta"? output-text edit-distance? embedding cosine? model perplexity?

kevin: good Q. proposal: two-tier check — cheap: embedding cosine on outputs (cost: 1 embedding per candidate). expensive: full token-delta on golden set run nightly or on canary. runtime uses embedding cos only.

tanya: embedding cos may miss subtle hallucinations. we should also monitor KL/perplexity drift vs baseline on a small streaming sample.

maria: also want per-layer activation stats for detecting catastrophic quantization on some layers. but that's heavier and probably opt-in for dedicated pools.

kevin: agreed — keep per-layer checks out of the hotpath. only enable per-layer mode for Dedicated or Debug runs. runtime fallback should be model-variant swap (e.g., fp8 -> int8 -> fp16) or route to a higher-tier pool.

sasha: API surface: runtime health hooks + a simple JSON config we can store per-model. something like:
```json
{"quant_sanity": {"golden_prompts_group": "short_help_text_v1", "embedding_cos_threshold": 0.86, "p95_delta_threshold": 0.12, "sampling_fraction": 0.01, "fallback_action": "swap_variant"}}
```

jordan: love that. where do we keep the golden prompts? git vs internal blobstore?

tanya: store in model-metadata blobstore with versioning + checksums. we should record a small hash of the expected outputs so we can cheaply detect drift without storing full text.

maria: operational note: sampling_fraction=0.01 for hosted, 0.1 for dedicated testing. need to ensure observability emits: sample_id, model_variant, embedding_score, fallback_triggered.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for model x-large with sampling=1% — watch metrics. :eyes:

kevin: fallback actions options: `swap_variant` (to a precompiled variant), `fallthrough_to_fp16` (force route), `reject_and_log`. prefer swap_variant + fallback counter so we can auto-roll back if many swaps occur.

sasha: one more tradeoff: embedding checks have false positives if outputs are paraphrases. need whitelist/relaxation rules per-prompt-type. e.g., summarization tasks should have lower threshold.

maria: good point — add `prompt_family` tags to golden set and thresholds per-family.

jordan: test plan: unit tests for the config parser, integration test that simulates a bad quantization (inject weight noise) and verifies fallback, smoke that verifies no more than 0.5% false-positive on canary traffic.

tanya: alerting: create alert when fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m or when embedding_score_median drops > 0.05. include runbook link.

kevin: who owns the rollout/task? I'll take the runtime hook + metric names. maria please own golden prompt selection and storage. sasha owns config schema and validation. jordan owns tests. tanya owns runbooks/alerts.

maria: acked. will prepare a 50-prompt seed and a script to compute baseline hashes.

sasha: i'll draft the JSON schema and a small lint that CI runs on model manifests.

jordan: i'll add an integration test that runs in the infra sandbox and simulates bad quant via a weight-perturbation flag.

kevin: timeline: ship canary next week, ramp to 5% after 48h if fallback_rate < 0.1%.

tanya: adding to oncall playbook now.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary finished — metrics look stable so far. :party_parrot:

kevin: awesome. followups: (1) decision doc w/ thresholds and why we chose embedding cos, (2) schema PR, (3) integration test PR. i'll open tickets.

sasha: quick note — we may want to expose a `force_bypass_sanity=true` flag for internal debug calls so we can test without triggering fallback.

maria: +1 for debug flag but guard with ACL.

kevin: cool. thanks everyone — this feels like a solid, minimal plan. we'll iterate after canary.
